title: Software
text: I write R packages for analyses that I run often, so that other people can repeat them. All of them are open source.

title: Software
text:
ggwas



ggwas draws plots for genome-wide association studies with ggplot2. It covers the usual steps from quality control to figures for a paper: Manhattan, QQ, Miami and locus zoom plots, PheWAS, fine-mapping, colocalization and genetic correlations. It includes journal themes and colour-blind-safe palettes, and it downsamples points so that biobank-sized files still plot quickly. The package is under review at Bioconductor.

 Code  Documentation  Zenodo DOI




ggwas in a few lines


pak::pak("bczech/ggwas")

library(ggwas)
data(example_gwas)  # columns CHR, BP, SNP, P

manhattan_plot(example_gwas)
qq_plot(example_gwas, show_lambda = TRUE)

title: Software
text:
BRASSVis
BRASSVis plots gene fusions and structural variants found by BRASS in whole-genome sequencing data. Each fusion gets one page with chromosome ideograms, exon structure, a circos plot, retained protein domains and read support. The layout follows the Arriba fusion plots, adapted to BRASS output.

I contribute to gDR, an open-source R suite for processing and analysing drug response screens, available on Bioconductor. It processed the screens behind the papers in Cancers (2024) and Nature Communications (2025).

title: Bartosz Czech, PhD, Eng.
text:
About
I am a bioinformatician and computational biologist. I analyse sequencing, mass spectrometry and drug screening data, build statistical models that answer biological questions, and write R packages and pipelines that make these analyses repeatable. My methods do not depend on the organism: I have worked with data from human cancer cell lines, cattle, chickens, cats, dog cells infected with influenza virus, and gut bacteria.

title: Bartosz Czech, PhD, Eng.
text:
Research




Sequencing data analysis
Whole-genome and targeted sequencing, variant calling, bulk and single-cell RNA-seq, small RNA-seq and 16S rRNA. I take the data from raw reads through quality control and alignment to statistical tests.





Multi-omics integration
Combining data types to explain one biological process, for example host gene expression with gut microbiome profiles. I also analyse mass spectrometry phosphoproteomics.





Statistical modelling and machine learning
Dose-response models for drug screens and drug combinations, mixed models and association studies, and supervised and unsupervised learning.

title: Research
text:
What I do
Sequencing data analysis. I analyse whole-genome, targeted and RNA sequencing data, including single-cell RNA-seq, small RNA-seq and 16S rRNA amplicons. I have built and run pipelines for variant calling, differential expression and small RNA annotation in many species: human cancer cells, cattle, chickens, cats, and dog cells infected with influenza A virus.
Multi-omics and microbiome data. I combine data types when one of them cannot explain a process alone, for example host RNA-seq with the gut microbiome. I also analyse mass spectrometry phosphoproteomics.
Statistical modelling and machine learning. I fit dose-response models to high-throughput drug screens, including drug combinations, run association studies with mixed models, and use machine learning for classification, such as separating true from false SNP calls or predicting semen quality after freezing.
Analysis choices and reproducibility. Reference genomes, pipelines and parameters can change the results of an analysis. I test how much they do, for example the effect of the reference transcriptome on cancer RNA-seq, and I package repeated analyses as R libraries and workflows.

Skills

Sequencing and omics data: WGS and WES, Variant calling, Structural variants and gene fusions, Bulk RNA-seq, Single-cell RNA-seq, Spatial transcriptomics (Visium HD), Small RNA-seq, ChIP-seq, ATAC-seq and scATAC-seq, Epigenomics, 16S rRNA and metagenomics, Genome annotation, Comparative and population genomics.
Drug discovery and proteomics: Dose-response modelling, Drug combinations and synergy, High-throughput screens, CRISPR screens, MS phosphoproteomics, Kinase activity (KSEA), Pathway and enrichment analysis, Network biology, Structural biology.
Statistics and machine learning: Linear and mixed models, GWAS and statistical genetics, Study design and power analysis, Multi-omics integration, Exploratory data analysis, Supervised and unsupervised learning, Deep learning, Feature engineering, scikit-learn, caret, TensorFlow and Keras, PyTorch.
Programming and visualisation: R, R packages (Bioconductor), Shiny, Python, Bash, sed, AWK, SQL, Git, GitHub, GitLab, ggplot2, Plotly, Seaborn, Dash, R Markdown and Quarto, Jupyter, LaTeX, REST APIs.
Pipelines, infrastructure and data: WDL pipelines, HPC and Slurm, Linux, AWS, Docker, Kubernetes, Conda, Snowflake, MySQL and SQLite, Database design, FAIR data, Metadata management.
Collaboration and delivery: Scrum, Product ownership, Jira, Trello, Reports for non-specialists, Scientific writing, Technical documentation, Teaching and training.
